sources.title: Go strings as arbitrary byte sequences
sources.sections_read: What is a string?; Printing strings; UTF-8 and string literals; Code points, characters, and runes; Range loops
sources.confirmed: Go strings can hold arbitrary bytes, including invalid UTF-8; indexing yields bytes and hexadecimal escapes can produce arbitrary values. Literal source characters and range iteration have UTF-8 semantics that must be distinguished from raw byte operations.
sources.limits: Unescaped non-ASCII source text becomes UTF-8, while range iteration decodes runes; byte indexing has different semantics. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C18.json.

sources.title: Python 3.3.5 bytes literals and byte sequences
sources.sections_read: String and bytes literals, escape sequences, footer date; fetched through unauthenticated urllib after web-tool error
sources.confirmed: Python 3.3.5 separates b/B-prefixed bytes literals from Unicode str, permits direct ASCII, and uses escapes for byte values at or above 128. The snapshot footer explicitly says it was last updated on March 9, 2014.
sources.limits: A one-byte literal still creates a sequence; indexing yields an integer, and direct non-ASCII source characters are disallowed. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C18.json.

sources.title: Racket 5.3.6 byte strings
sources.version_or_date: Racket 5.3.6; August 2013 release verified by the official all-versions table
sources.confirmed: Racket represents individual bytes as integers from 0 to 255 and byte strings with a # prefix, readable ASCII, and escaped non-ASCII values. Byte-string output writes bytes without Unicode encoding; conversions to text require an explicit encoding.
sources.limits: Individual bytes are integers from 0 to 255; character conversion needs an explicitly selected encoding. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C18.json.

sources.title: Erlang bit syntax
sources.version_or_date: live Erlang/OTP 29.1.2 documentation; publication date not supplied
sources.sections_read: Introduction; Examples; Segments; Defaults; Constructing Binaries and Bitstrings
sources.confirmed: Erlang bit syntax constructs and matches byte or bit sequences with readable string segments, integers, explicit field sizes, signedness, and endianness. Integer segments default to eight bits.
sources.limits: This is a richer binary construction mechanism; field sizes, byte alignment, and endianness require deliberate choices. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C18.json.

sources.sections_read: Targeted find for Character literals; sections 6.1 and 6.2.1 returned by find (conservatively counted as a further page retrieval)

sources.limits: Upper byte values have Latin-1 character semantics; transfer the notation separately from Rust's existing Unicode character and string types.
